title: Pupils plant 600 mangroves to protect village
text:
By Rina Saputra

Primary school pupils in the fishing village of Tanjung Harapan planted 600 mangrove seedlings along the shore on Saturday, in a project to protect homes from rising waves.

Sixty pupils from Class 5 at SD Pelita Bangsa worked in pairs, wading through knee-deep mud to push each seedling firmly into the ground. Local fishermen helped by marking the planting area with bamboo poles at low tide.

The project was the idea of eleven-year-old Aditya Ramadhan, who noticed last year that waves were reaching the path outside his grandmother’s house. “The sea is coming closer every year,” he explained. “Our teacher told us that mangrove roots can slow down waves, so we decided to try.”

The school raised Rp2.500.000 for seedlings by holding a book sale and a cooking competition, and a local plant nursery gave another 100 seedlings as a gift.

Pak Hendra Wijaya, who has fished in the area for thirty years, welcomed the project. “When I was a boy, there were mangroves all along this coast and we caught plenty of crabs,” he said. “After the trees were cut down, the crabs disappeared. I hope these young trees will bring them back.”

Experts warn that new mangroves need careful protection. Seedlings can be washed away by strong waves or eaten by goats, and it can take several years before the trees are big enough to protect the shore.

The pupils already have a plan. Each class will visit the site once a month to check the seedlings, replace any that have died and pick up rubbish that could harm them.

“It will take time,” said head teacher Ibu Maya Kusuma. “But in ten years, when these trees are taller than our pupils, the whole village will feel the difference.”
